Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the Q&A are to press star then one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Investment Officer; and Lisa Chen, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust organic growth, strong client retention, and meaningful net inflows across our platforms. Our AUM grew to $1.35 trillion.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $906 million, representing an 18% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by 12% AUM expansion, higher average market levels, and a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin alternatives, despite modest fee compression. Our total expenses were carefully managed at $550 million, reflecting prudent cost discipline, resulting in net income of $285 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently, and I'll now dive deeper into some key aspects.

Let me start with our compensation ratio, which came in at 47.2% for the quarter, down 320 basis points year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially from Q2's 47.7%. For the full nine months, it's averaged 48.1%, a meaningful improvement from 52.4% in the same period last year. This metric—compensation expense as a percentage of revenue—remains a core focus for us, as it directly reflects our operating leverage in an industry where human capital drives alpha generation and client retention.

To contextualize, our total compensation expense was $428 million in the quarter, up just 2% year-over-year, while revenue grew to that $906 million figure I mentioned, fueled by AUM growth to $1.2 trillion on average, elevated markets, and the mix shift I noted. Breaking it down, fixed compensation—salaries and benefits—accounted for 62% of the total, holding steady at $265 million, while variable comp, including bonuses and long-term incentives, was 38% or $163 million. This discipline underscores our pay-for-performance culture, where over 70% of senior portfolio manager pay is now at-risk, tied to three-year net performance attribution versus benchmarks like the S&P 500 or MSCI World.

Year-over-year trends are encouraging. Back in Q3 2023, the ratio spiked to 50.5% amid aggressive talent acquisition during the post-pandemic hiring wave—we added 180 heads in research and distribution to scale our active equity and private markets platforms. Revenue then was softer at $745 million, pressured by outflows in core long-only strategies amid the regional bank scare and rising rates. Fast-forward to today: AUM inflows of $28 billion in Q3, led by $15 billion into our Apex Alternatives suite—think our evergreen private credit fund yielding 9-11% net IRR—and ETF launches like the Apex ESG Global Equity ETF, which has gathered $4.2 billion since inception in H1. This revenue expansion, coupled with 4% headcount optimization through natural attrition and reallocations, delivered the deleveraging.

Regionally, dynamics vary. In the Americas, which represent 65% of our revenue, the ratio sits at a lean 45.8%, benefiting from scale in our BlackRock-competitive iShares-like ETF business and Vanguard-style low-cost indexing. We've held headcount flat here while ramping quant capabilities—our new AI-driven alpha overlay tool, Apex AlphaForge, now covers 40% of our $450 billion equity AUM, reducing reliance on traditional analysts by 15% without sacrificing Sharpe ratios above 1.2. EMEA, at 22% of revenue, saw a ratio of 51.3%, elevated due to MiFID II unbundling costs and talent premiums—portfolio managers in London command 20% more than U.S. peers to compete with Amundi and UBS AM. That said, we're mitigating via localized variable pay caps linked to UCITS-compliant flows, which turned positive at €5 billion for the quarter. APAC, our growth engine at 13% of revenue, clocks in at 49.7%, pressured by hiring in Singapore and Tokyo for mandarin-speaking specialists in our Greater China quant strategies. But with AUM up 22% there on yen carry trade unwind and Indian equity tailwinds, we expect compression to 47% by year-end.

Strategically, we're benchmarking against peers like T. Rowe Price, with their typical 46-48% ratios, and Fidelity, around 50%, but with our alternatives mix—now 28% of AUM versus the industry's 20% average—we have structural tailwinds. Performance fees from our closed-end PE funds, like Apex Venture Partners II, vintage 2021, which delivered 2.5x DPI, contributed $85 million this quarter, allowing us to flex variable comp without ratio erosion. Initiatives include our 2024 Comp Framework refresh: introducing clawbacks aligned with SEC private fund rules, escalating equity grants to 40% of total comp for PMs, vesting over four years with performance hurdles, and a DEI-linked bonus pool that rewarded our 35% women in investment roles. Technically, we're piloting blockchain-based incentive tracking via partnership with Fidelity Digital Assets, ensuring transparent attribution in tokenized real estate funds.

Looking ahead, we guide to a full-year ratio of 47.5-48.5%, assuming AUM growth to $1.35 trillion by year-end and stable markets. Risks include further fee pressure—industry basis points dipped to 32 from 35 pre-2022 on passive ETF dominance—but we're countering with product innovation like our target-date ESG funds, projected at 25 bps with $10 billion potential. Upside from volatility harvesting in our risk premia strategies, akin to AQR's approach, could accelerate variable pay deferrals.

In sum, this ratio improvement validates our focus on scalable talent models amid industry headwinds like redemptions in active U.S. large-cap and regulatory scrutiny on 40 Act fees. We're positioning Apex for mid-teens ROE expansion, prioritizing client alpha over short-term comp inflation.

Now, shifting to another key growth engine: client retention rates and new client acquisition. In an industry where fee compression from giants like BlackRock and Vanguard continues to squeeze margins—now averaging just 28 basis points on passive ETFs—and where net flows have been bifurcated toward low-cost index products amid the post-2022 equity rebound, our performance here stands out. We delivered record organic growth in Q3, with net client inflows of $14.2 billion, up 22% year-over-year, bringing our total AUM to $1.35 trillion as of quarter-end.

Retention remains our bedrock. Our annualized client retention rate held steady at 96.8%—the highest in our peer group per Morningstar data—compared to the industry benchmark of 92-94% for diversified managers like T. Rowe Price or Fidelity. This metric, calculated on a dollar-weighted basis across our 18,000 institutional and HNW client relationships, reflects not just inertia but active stickiness. For context, institutional retention was an exceptional 98.2%, driven by our defined benefit pension mandates, where we've locked in multi-year commitments averaging 7.5 years. On the intermediary side—wealth platforms like Schwab and Morgan Stanley—retention dipped slightly to 95.1% due to some tactical reallocations into high-yield fixed income amid Fed rate cut expectations, but we clawed back 85% of those via cross-selling our active fixed income strategies.

What underpinned this resilience? First, our holistic wallet share expansion: we grew average client wallet penetration from 14% to 17% YoY by leveraging data analytics to identify untapped opportunities. For instance, our proprietary Client360 platform, powered by AI-driven predictive modeling akin to what State Street uses in its Alpha suite, flagged 1,200 cross-sell opportunities in Q3, converting 62% into new mandates—adding $3.8 billion in AUM. Second, ESG integration has been a retention booster; 72% of retained clients now allocate to our sustainable strategies, up from 55% last year, aligning with the $40 trillion global sustainable AUM milestone per BloombergNEF. We saw zero churn in our Climate Transition ETF suite, even as broader active equity outflows hit $200 billion industry-wide in H1.

Regionally, performance was robust. In the Americas, which represent 62% of our AUM, retention ticked up to 97.3% on strong U.S. RIA channel loyalty—our Advisor Portal upgrades, including real-time performance attribution and seamless SMA onboarding, reduced administrative friction by 40%. EMEA retention at 96.2% benefited from MiFID II-compliant transparency tools, helping us retain £5.2 billion in UK DC pension flows despite outflows at peers like Legal & General. APAC lagged slightly at 95.4%, pressured by China's property sector woes and yen volatility, but we offset this with 15% YoY growth in Korean sovereign wealth mandates.

Turning to new client acquisition, we netted 1,450 new relationships in Q3, a 28% increase QoQ, generating $18.5 billion in gross inflows—our strongest quarter since the 2021 alternatives boom. Organic flows represented 89% of this, underscoring the efficacy of our go-to-market strategy. Breakdown by channel: institutional wins totaled $9.1 billion, including a landmark $4.2 billion private credit mandate from a Nordic SWF, tapping into the $1.7 trillion dry powder per Preqin data. Retail and intermediary flows hit $9.4 billion, fueled by our ETF lineup—launches like the Apex Active ESG Equity ETF gathered $2.8 billion in its first full quarter, outpacing Vanguard's equivalent by 3x on AUM growth.

Key trends driving acquisition: the great wealth transfer, projected at $84 trillion over the next 20 years per Cerulli Associates, has supercharged our next-gen HNW focus. We acquired 320 family office relationships via targeted outreach, emphasizing our ultra-high-net-worth alternatives platform targeting 15-20% IRRs in secondaries and direct lending. Digitally, our robo-hybrid advisor tool—blending Vanguard-like automation with human oversight—onboarded 45,000 new retail clients, capturing 12% market share in the U.S. direct indexing space per Coalition Greenwich.

Strategically, we're doubling down on three pillars for FY24 acceleration. One, tech-led personalization: rolling out GenAI chat interfaces for portfolio construction by Q1, piloted with 500 beta clients to boost conversion rates 25%. Two, alternatives dominance: targeting $50 billion in new alts flows via co-investments with KKR and Apollo, capitalizing on the 18% CAGR in private markets per McKinsey. Three, geographic expansion: a $100 million commitment to APAC distribution, including a JV with a Japanese megabank to penetrate JGB replacement strategies amid BOJ normalization.

Looking forward, we guide to $60-70 billion in net inflows for FY24, implying 5-6% organic AUM growth excluding markets. Risks include potential tariff escalations impacting cross-border flows and persistent fee pressure, but our 15% operating margin expansion gives us firepower for selective M&A—like our recent $2.5 billion tuck-in of a boutique quant shop.

Next, I'll turn to our organic growth rate and market share dynamics, which continue to underscore the strength of our franchise. As a reminder, we define organic AUM growth as the change in assets driven by net new money—gross client inflows minus redemptions and withdrawals—excluding market appreciation, foreign exchange impacts, and any structural changes like acquisitions. This metric isolates our ability to win and retain client mandates through product performance, client service, and distribution excellence.

For Q3, we delivered organic net inflows of $18.2 billion, bringing our nine-month total to $42.7 billion. This translates to an organic growth rate of 7.8% quarter-over-quarter and a robust 12.4% year-over-year on a trailing 12-month basis, outpacing the industry average of 4.2% as reported by Morningstar Direct. Our total AUM now stands at $1.35 trillion, up 14% from the prior year, with organic flows accounting for over 60% of that expansion. This performance reflects not just favorable market tailwinds but our disciplined execution in a fee-compressed, passive-dominated landscape.

Breaking it down by key segments, where we've seen differentiated strength: Equities saw organic inflows of $9.4 billion in Q3, driving a 9.2% YoY organic growth rate. Our passive equity ETFs, including the flagship Apex S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF with $45 billion in AUM, captured $6.8 billion in net new money—up 25% from Q3 2023. This was fueled by retail platforms like Schwab and Fidelity, where we gained 30 basis points of market share in large-cap passive strategies, now holding 2.8% overall versus Vanguard's 28% dominance. Actively managed equities added $2.6 billion, benefiting from our quant-enhanced strategies, which have outperformed the MSCI World Index by 180 basis points net over three years.

Fixed income posted $4.1 billion in organic inflows, a 6.5% YoY growth rate, amid heightened volatility from Fed rate cut expectations. Short-duration and ESG-focused bond funds, such as our Apex Green Bond ETF at $22 billion AUM, drew $2.9 billion, gaining 45 basis points of share in sustainable fixed income to 1.9%. Institutional wins here included a $1.2 billion mandate from a European pension fund, offsetting some outflows in longer-duration products as yields normalized.

Alternatives and multi-asset shone brightest, with $4.7 billion in inflows and a stellar 18.3% YoY organic growth rate. Our private credit and infrastructure platforms, totaling $180 billion in AUM, secured $3.2 billion from sovereign wealth funds and family offices. Notably, our Apex Infrastructure Debt Fund II closed at $15 billion, exceeding its target by 20%. Multi-asset solutions, like our target-date series, added $1.5 billion, capturing share from target-date competitors amid DC plan consolidations.

Regionally, our diversification is paying off. In the Americas, 62% of AUM, we saw $11.5 billion in organic inflows—a 13% YoY increase—driven by wirehouse channels and 401(k) platforms. Europe contributed $4.8 billion, up 22% YoY, with strong uptake in UCITS ETFs following MiFID II refinements; we've gained 60 basis points in continental passive equities to 3.2% share. APAC, now 12% of AUM, delivered $1.9 billion, a 35% surge, thanks to our Hong Kong platform expansion and a landmark $800 million mandate from a Japanese GPIF allocator. Emerging markets remain a growth vector, with organic flows up 28% in LatAm via local currency bond strategies.

On market share, we're methodically expanding our footprint. Per eVestment and Preqin data, we've increased our global institutional market share by 25 basis points to 2.4% in long-only mandates, and 40 basis points to 1.7% in alternatives—chipping away at leaders like BlackRock's 18% institutional share and Amundi. In retail ETFs, our 1.5% U.S. share grew by 15 basis points, propelled by iShares and Vanguard fee wars, where our average ETF fee of 12 bps remains competitive. We've also clawed back 20 basis points in high-net-worth multi-asset from competitors like PIMCO amid their redemption pressures.

Key drivers? Product innovation: We've launched five new ETFs YTD, including an active semi-transparent ETF leveraging our proprietary AlphaForge AI model, which has already amassed $1.2 billion. Distribution firepower: Partnerships with Aladdin and Charles River have streamlined institutional onboarding, reducing time-to-market by 40%. Client retention: Our net flow retention rate hit 95%, bolstered by personalized ESG analytics via our Apex Insight platform. Fee compression is a headwind—blended fees dipped 3 bps to 32 bps—but we're countering with scale and higher-margin alts, now 15% of AUM.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 organic growth of 8-10%, supported by $25 billion in pipeline, including a potential $5 billion U.S. endowment win. Strategically, we're doubling down on tech-enabled personalization—rolling out gen-AI portfolio constructors for RIAs—and APAC localization, targeting 20% regional growth via Mumbai and Sydney hubs. Risks include equity derating or geopolitical flares, but our 70/30 active/passive mix and $200 billion cash alternatives buffer position us resiliently.

Finally, on assets under management, which remain a cornerstone of our long-term growth story. Ending AUM for Q3 stood at $1.35 trillion, up 20.8% year-over-year from roughly $1.12 trillion at the end of Q3 last year, and 4.2% quarter-over-quarter from Q2. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outpacing the industry average of 12% YoY as reported by Morningstar Direct.

Our AUM growth decomposes into three key drivers: market and performance appreciation contributed $112 billion or 62% of the YoY increase, reflecting broad equity rallies and modest fixed income gains; net client inflows—or NNM—added $78 billion, up 35% from the prior-year quarter; and FX translation effects chipped in the remaining $20 billion, largely from a strengthening euro and yen against the dollar.

Drilling into the asset class breakdown, which highlights our diversified platform: Equities, 47% of total AUM at $602 billion, grew 28% YoY and 6.1% QoQ. This was fueled by $45 billion in NNM into our active and passive equity strategies, including our flagship Apex S&P 500 ETF, which saw $12 billion in inflows amid the index's 22% total return. Performance attribution was strong, with our large-cap growth mandates outperforming the Russell 1000 Growth Index by 150 basis points, thanks to overweight positions in AI leaders like NVIDIA and Microsoft. We also benefited from tactical allocations to emerging markets equities, up 15% in AUM to $85 billion, driven by India and Brazil exposure.

Fixed income, at 31% of AUM or $397 billion, expanded 12% YoY and 2.8% QoQ. While duration extension in core bond strategies tempered gains amid the Fed's 50 bps rate cut in September, we saw resilient inflows of $22 billion, particularly into our short-duration and municipal bond products. Our Apex Ultra-Short Treasury ETF gathered $8 billion in NNM as clients sought yield—yielding 5.2% annualized. Credit strategies, including high-yield and EM debt, added $15 billion, benefiting from spread tightening.

Alternatives, now 18% of AUM at $230 billion, surged 32% YoY and 5.5% QoQ, underscoring our leadership in this high-margin segment. NNM here was exceptional at $28 billion, led by private credit and real assets. Our evergreen private equity fund-of-funds closed two vintages totaling $10 billion, capitalizing on dislocation in direct lending. Real estate AUM hit $45 billion, up 40%, with opportunistic buys in logistics and data centers. Hedge fund-like strategies, including our quant macro pod, returned 12% net YTD, outpacing the HFRI Fund Weighted Composite.

Multi-asset and cash equivalents at 4% or $51 billion grew modestly 8% YoY, serving as a low-volatility buffer with $3 billion in inflows.

Regionally, growth was broad-based. North America remains our anchor at 58% of AUM ($742 billion, +22% YoY), but EMEA accelerated to 25% ($320 billion, +26% YoY) on DC pension inflows into our ESG equity sleeves, compliant with SFDR Article 8/9 standards. Asia-Pacific now at 15% ($192 billion, +18% YoY) benefited from MPF mandates in Hong Kong and our new Tokyo-domiciled UCITS feeder into alternatives. LatAm rounded out at 2%, with steady growth in Brazil via local FI strategies.

From a technical standpoint, our initiatives are paying off. We launched three new ETFs in Q3—Apex Green Bond ETF, Equity Income 2.0, and Crypto-Linked Alternatives—deploying Aladdin-derived analytics for real-time liquidity management, reducing tracking error to under 5 bps. Our digital client portal, ApexOne, now has 1.2 million users, driving 40% of retail NNM organically. On the institutional side, we're embedding climate risk modeling via our partnership with MSCI, enhancing stickiness in $200 billion of sustainable mandates.

These results affirm our 'Diversify, Digitize, and Deliver' framework. With alternatives now over 20% of flows—up from 12% two years ago—we're targeting 25-30% fee compression-resistant revenue from this segment by 2026. Amid potential volatility from U.S. elections and China stimulus, we're positioning for 15-18% long-term AUM CAGR through 2027, with NNM guidance of $80-100 billion annually.

With that detailed financial overview, I'll hand it back.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in alternatives, where we navigated the current market environment by increasing allocations to private credit and infrastructure amid persistent yield-seeking behavior. We are leveraging our AlphaForge AI tool across 40% of equity mandates to enhance alpha without added risk. We launched the Apex ESG Global Equity ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $4.2 billion in assets already, demonstrating demand for our sustainable active strategies that have beaten the MSCI World ESG Leaders Index by 220 basis points since inception.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by $1.9 billion in regional organic flows, up 35% year-over-year, driven by partnerships like our JV with a Japanese megabank and robust retail uptake via digital platforms in Hong Kong and Singapore.

Johnathan Hale: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes scaling our alternatives platform to 25% of AUM, accelerating tech-driven personalization, and pursuing disciplined M&A to bolster our quant and ESG capabilities.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs.

David Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your impressive organic growth rate this quarter?

Johnathan Hale: Thanks, David. Absolutely, our 7.8% QoQ organic growth was propelled by strength across equities, fixed income, and especially alternatives, where we saw 18.3% YoY growth. Product innovation like our new ETFs and strong performance in quant strategies helped us gain market share, as Sarah detailed. It's a testament to our diversified approach in a challenging environment.

David Lee: Thank you. And a follow-up on the compensation ratio—how sustainable is that improvement, especially with APAC hiring pressures?

Sarah Jenkins: Great question, David. The 47.2% ratio is sustainable through our pay-for-performance model and headcount optimization. In APAC, despite 49.7% regionally, we're seeing compression from 22% AUM growth there, and our full-year guide of 47.5-48.5% factors in that. Variable pay tied to three-year performance keeps us aligned.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Thompson with Morningstar.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning. I wanted to dive into the flows story this quarter. Total net flows came in at $12.4 billion—strong beat on consensus—but could you walk us through the drivers, breakdowns by asset class and channel, and any regional color? Also, how are you thinking about the sustainability of this amid the rate cut cycle?

Sarah Jenkins: Great question, Sarah, and thanks for the shoutout on the beat. Let me unpack our Q3 total net flows of $12.4 billion, which mark our strongest quarter since Q4 2021 and represent a 28% YoY increase from $9.7 billion last year. This organic growth—now running at a 4.1% annualized rate on average AUM of $1.18 trillion—continues to outpace the industry average of 2.8% as reported by Morningstar Direct, underscoring our positioning in high-conviction growth areas like passive ETFs and alternatives.

Starting with the headline breakdown by product suite: ETFs led the charge with $8.2 billion in net inflows, up 35% QoQ. Our iShares-inspired core equity ETFs, particularly the Apex S&P 500 UCITS ETF and the new Apex Nasdaq-100 ESG ETF launched in June, captured $5.1 billion alone. Retail investors piled in amid the AI-driven tech rally, with the Nasdaq ETF seeing 22% MoM inflow acceleration. Institutional flows here were bolstered by our model portfolio integrations with platforms like Envestnet and Orion, adding $1.4 billion.

Active managed products saw $2.9 billion in inflows, a solid rebound from Q2. Our flagship Apex Global Equity Alpha strategy reversed prior outflows with $1.8 billion, thanks to alpha generation of 450 bps over the benchmark YTD. Fixed income active strategies added $0.7 billion, driven by our short-duration credit funds amid peak Fed funds uncertainty.

Alternatives and multi-asset contributed $1.8 billion, with private credit funds like Apex Direct Lending Partners V pulling in $1.2 billion from pension plans and sovereign wealth funds. This reflects the 15% CAGR in alts demand, as clients seek 7-9% yields in a post-ZIRP world.

On the flip side, we had modest outflows of $0.5 billion from legacy long-duration bond mutual funds—consistent with industry trends where active fixed income has seen $250 billion in YTD outflows per ICI data—partially offset by $0.3 billion in retirement channel stickiness via our target-date series.

By channel: Retail and RIA flows hit a record $6.8 billion, or 55% of total, fueled by our Apex WealthTech platform, which now serves 2.4 million direct accounts with AI-driven personalization—up 18% YoY. Institutional netted $4.1 billion, 33%, with wins from three top-20 US pensions totaling $2.2 billion, favoring our evergreen interval funds. HNW and family offices rounded out at $1.5 billion.

Regionally, this was truly global: Americas, 72% of flows at $8.9 billion, dominated by US retail into ETFs, plus Canadian DB plans adding $900 million to alts amid OSFI Solvency II pressures. EMEA, 18% or $2.2 billion: strong UCITS ETF uptake in the UK and Germany, with €1.1 billion into our sustainable equity range post-SFDR reclassification. APAC, 10% or $1.3 billion: record quarter with $800 million from Japanese GPIF-like mandates into our yen-hedged equity ETFs and $400 million retail from our WeChat mini-app in China.

Key trends: the great wealth transfer—$84 trillion globally per Cerulli—favors our low-cost ETF wrappers at average 12 bps. ESG remains resilient; 42% of inflows, $5.2 billion, qualified as Article 8/9 under SFDR. Our digital initiatives—like the beta launch of Apex AI Portfolio Optimizer—drove 25% of retail flows via Schwab and Fidelity integrations.

Strategically, for flow acceleration into 2025: product innovation with five new active ETFs in Q4, including a US Small Cap Value targeting 6% yield; distribution expansion via Aladdin and India JV with HDFC AMC; fee optimization blending active alpha with passive scale at 32 bps blended.

We see $50-60 billion in full-year flows, assuming no recession, with upside from 50-75 bps Fed cuts. We're well-positioned versus T. Rowe's flat flows or Fidelity's alts lag, thanks to our 60/40 passive/active mix.

Sarah, does that cover it, or want more on the alts pipeline?

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
